question:
A 43-year-old male patient with a history of disc herniation surgery 8 years prior presents to the
osteopathic clinic for chronic low back pain that has previously responded well to OMT. Your structural
examination reveals a left innominate rotation with the left posterior superior iliac spine positioned
higher than the right. A seated flexion test yields positive results on the left side. You decide to use
muscle energy technique as your initial treatment approach for this somatic dysfunction. What is the
correct patient positioning for this treatment? Answer Choices: (A) Right lateral decubitus with left leg
extended (B) Standing with weight shifted to the right leg (C) Supine with both hips and knees flexed
symmetrically (D) Lying on their left side, hips and knees flexed with both legs off the table (E) Left
lateral Sims position with both legs off the table (F) Supine with right hip and knee flexed until
resistance is felt (G) Prone position with left knee flexed to 90 degrees (H) Prone with bilateral knee
flexion to 90 degrees (I) Sitting with legs dangling off the table (J) Lying supine, left hip and knee flexed
until resistance is felt
 A. Supine with both hips and knees flexed symmetrically
B. Lying on their left side, hips and knees flexed with both legs off the table
C. Right lateral decubitus with left leg extended
D. Left lateral Sims position with both legs off the table
E. Sitting with legs dangling off the table
F. Standing with weight shifted to the right leg
G. Supine with right hip and knee flexed until resistance is felt
H. Lying supine, left hip and knee flexed until resistance is felt
I. Prone position with left knee flexed to 90 degrees
J. Prone with bilateral knee flexion to 90 degrees
